info.title: Loaner Pool API
info.description:
Device inventory, barcode check-out and check-in, loan tracking, counselor requests, audit and reporting for an assistive technology loaner pool.

## Authentication

Two schemes, both producing the same permission model:

- **API key** (`Authorization: Bearer lp_<prefix>_<secret>`) — for integrations. Create keys under Settings → API keys. The plaintext is shown once and stored only as a hash.
- **Session cookie** — used by the browser client. Not intended for third-party use.

## Scopes

| Scope   | Can do                                                        |
|---------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| `read`  | List and view devices, loans, requests, clients, programs, reports |
| `write` | Everything `read` can, plus check-out/check-in, create and edit records, approve requests |
| `admin` | Everything, including settings, staff accounts and API keys    |

## Errors

Every error uses the same envelope:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "conflict", "message": "Human readable explanation.", "details": { } } }
```

`message` is written to be shown to an end user. `code` is stable and safe to branch on. `details` carries machine-readable context such as the offending `field`.

## Pagination

List endpoints accept `page` and `per_page` (max 200) and return:

```json
{ "data": [ ], "meta": { "page": 1, "per_page": 50, "total": 132, "total_pages": 3 } }
```

## Rate limiting

None is enforced by the application. If you expose this to the internet, rate limit at the reverse proxy.

post.description:
A device may be held by any combination of a technician, a client and a program; at least one is required by default. `device` accepts a scanned barcode, an asset tag or a numeric device id, so the scanner, typed and pick-from-list paths behave identically.

Concurrency is handled with a row lock, so two simultaneous check-outs of the same device cannot both succeed.

loan_period_id.description: Omit to use the organisation default.

get.description: Cancelled loans are excluded throughout, since a loan cancelled because the wrong barcode was scanned is not a use of the device. `total_days_out` counts open loans up to now, so a device out for six months is not reported as zero until it returns.

Secrets are never returned; each is replaced by an `__is_set` flag and a masked hint.

patch.description: Unknown keys are ignored and reported rather than stored. A secret sent as an empty string is left unchanged, so saving a form with a masked field cannot wipe it; send `__CLEAR__` to remove one.

200.description: Updated, with the list of keys that changed

`days: 0` creates an open-ended period with no due date.

delete.description: The devices in it are unaffected and keep their history.

post.description: Issues one loan per device under a shared `group_ref`, so the "one active loan per device" invariant still holds and each unit keeps its own history. Members that are unavailable are reported in `skipped` rather than failing the whole kit — a partly issued kit that says so is more useful at the desk than an all-or-nothing error.

put.description: Accessories are a checklist on the device, not tracked items with their own barcodes — a charger is what goes missing, but is not worth its own asset record.

post.description: Each device is returned independently; failures are reported per device.

get.description: Counselors see only their own. `queue_position` is computed from (priority DESC, created_at ASC) and never stored, so it cannot drift.

post.description: Wait for one specific device, or for the next available device of a category. If something matching is free right now, the response says so in `available_now` rather than silently queueing behind nothing.
Any device being held is released and offered to the next person in the queue.

patch.description: Closing returns the device to the pool. Closing as `unrepairable` retires it instead, so broken equipment never goes back into circulation. A closed repair cannot be reopened — open a new one, so each fault keeps its own history.

The wording for a loan, with placeholders filled in
The signed agreement for a loan

409.description: This loan already has a signed agreement

post.description:
Four methods, all equal: `typed` (name as attestation), `drawn` (canvas image), `uploaded` (photo of a signed paper form) and `waived` (with a reason). Drawing is a dragging interaction, so offering the alternatives is what keeps this step reachable for someone who cannot use a pointer.

The wording is snapshotted onto the loan at signing time — later edits to the template never alter what somebody signed. One signature per loan; it cannot be replaced.

get.description: HTML rather than PDF: it prints identically, needs no PDF dependency on shared hosting, and can be read by a screen reader.

get.summary: Stream a stored photo or signature
get.description: Authenticated and organisation-scoped. Files live outside the web root and are never at a guessable URL.

403.description: Condition photos are disabled for this organisation

post.description: Images arrive as base64 data URLs, resized by the browser first. Magic bytes are checked, not just the declared type. Partial success is reported rather than thrown: photos are optional, so one unreadable image must not fail the rest.

post.summary: Check in many devices at once
post.description: Each is attempted independently and the response reports both sides. At the end of a program twenty devices come back and one turns out not to be on loan — failing all twenty because of that one is unusable.

post.summary: Change the status of many devices
post.description: Devices currently on loan are skipped and reported.

get.description: `healthy` is false when the reminder job has not completed successfully in the last 36 hours — which is how you find out reminders stopped going out.

post.description: Authenticated either by an administrator session or by an `X-Cron-Token` header, since a cron entry cannot hold a cookie. Safe to run concurrently: a loan chased in the last day is excluded by the query itself.

get.summary: Utilisation and spend by funding source
get.description: Device-level and loan-level figures are aggregated separately. Summing purchase cost across a loan join would multiply each device's price by how often it was lent, overstating every number a funder is shown.

post.description: Always reports success, whether or not the address exists — anything else turns this into a way of enumerating staff. Tokens are single-use, stored only as a hash, and expire in an hour.

post.description: Ends every session the account holds.

ApiKeyAuth.description: An API key in the form `lp_<prefix>_<secret>`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state

message.description: Written to be shown to an end user.

details.description: Machine-readable context, such as the offending `field`.

barcode.description: Globally unique. This is what a scanner reads.

current_holder.description: Derived. Who has it right now.

is_overdue.description: Derived from the active loan's due date.

custom_fields.description: Spreadsheet columns that did not map to a known field.

holder_summary.description: Derived one-line description of who holds the device.

due_at.description: Null means an open-ended loan with no return date.

is_overdue.description: Derived, never stored — a row can never sit at 'active' while silently months overdue.
